To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Big Five personality traits are significantly correlated with sales performance, and that the relationship between personality traits and sales performance is influenced by leadership style.

(1) The relationship between salesperson personality and sales performance is moderated by leadership style; (2) The Big Five personality traits, except Emotional Stability, have significant effects on sales performance; (3) Leadership styles of transformational and transactional have positive effects on sales performance, while laissez-faire style has negative effects on sales performance.
The Big Five personality factors, Emotional Stability, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Conscientious, have positive effects on sales performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two research questions: 1.
the following issues: (a) the relationship between personality factors (Big Five) and sales performance; (b) the moderating effects of leadership style on the personality-performance relationship.
the relationship between the personality traits of salespersons and their sales performance, with the moderating effects of leadership style.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
personality-performance relationship is not a static, one-dimensional relationship.
leadership is a critical factor in determining salespeople's performance.

the relationship between personality traits and performance is not a simple and direct one, but a more complex and indirect one, and leadership style is one factor that may influence the personality-performance relationship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Big Five personality factors are important predictors of job performance in sales.
the relationship between personality traits and job performance is not a simple one, but is moderated by a variety of exogenous factors.
leadership is an important situational factor that moderates the personality-performance relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the relationship between personality traits and job performance is moderated by situational factors, in particular leadership style, and that the moderating effect can be different for each of the five factors, as well as the job performance outcome.
the personality-performance relationship can be moderated by situational variables, and that leadership style is one example of such a situational variable.
the personality traits that are associated with job performance in the absence of leadership are not necessarily the traits that are associated when leadership is considered.
